findings.title: Load balancer internet-facing
findings.description: A load balancer with internal absent or false is internet-facing (false is the provider default). Internet-facing LBs widen the attack surface and should be a deliberate choice.

findings.title: Load balancer listener uses plain HTTP
findings.description: A listener terminating plain HTTP sends credentials and session tokens in cleartext. Listeners should use HTTPS (or TLS) with a certificate.

findings.title: Load balancer not dropping invalid headers
findings.description: Without drop_invalid_header_fields, malformed HTTP headers reach targets and enable request-smuggling style attacks. The provider default is false.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Load balancer without deletion protection
findings.description: Without enable_deletion_protection, a load balancer can be destroyed by a single API call or Terraform change, taking the service offline. The provider default is disabled.

findings.title: Load balancer without access logs
findings.description: Access logs record every request to the load balancer and are essential for incident response and forensics. Enable them with an access_logs block pointing at an S3 bucket.
findings.remediation: Enable audit logging. Turn on CloudTrail (multi-region, log file validation, KMS-encrypted bucket), VPC flow logs, and service access logs. Ship logs to a dedicated, MFA-delete-protected bucket in a security account.

findings.title: Public load balancer without WAF
findings.description: An internet-facing load balancer with no WAFv2 web ACL association is exposed to common web exploits, bots, and application-layer DDoS with no managed filtering in front of it.

evidence.expected: internal = true, or an aws_wafv2_web_acl_association on this load balancer

findings.remediation: Remove public exposure. Restrict ingress to known CIDR ranges, move the resource into private subnets, and front it with a load balancer or API gateway if external access is required. Verify with `aws ec2 describe-security-groups`.

findings.title: Load balancer listener without HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect
findings.description: A port-80 listener whose default_action does not redirect to HTTPS serves traffic in plaintext instead of upgrading clients to an encrypted connection.
findings.remediation: Enforce TLS 1.2+. Replace HTTP listeners with HTTPS, set a modern TLS policy (e.g. `ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06`), and redirect HTTP→HTTPS. Disable weak ciphers and old protocol versions everywhere.

findings.title: Load balancer without access logging
findings.description: Hygiene: Load balancers should log access to S3 for traffic analysis and incident investigation. Add an access_logs block with a bucket.
findings.remediation: Enable audit logging. Turn on CloudTrail (multi-region, log file validation, KMS-encrypted bucket), VPC flow logs, and service access logs. Ship logs to a dedicated, MFA-delete-protected bucket in a security account.
